MOLECULAR GENETICS LABORATORY REPORT
[redacted location] Medical Center
Department of Clinical Genetics

PATIENT: [redacted name]
DATE OF BIRTH: [redacted date]
MEDICAL RECORD: [redacted ID]
SPECIMEN TYPE: Placental tissue (uncultured)
DATE COLLECTED: [redacted date]
DATE RECEIVED: [redacted date]
DATE REPORTED: [redacted date]

CLINICAL INDICATION
Fetal loss investigation

TEST PERFORMED
Quantitative Fluorescence Polymerase Chain Reaction (QF-PCR) for Rapid Aneuploidy Detection

METHOD
QF-PCR analysis was performed on uncultured placental material to detect aneuploidies of chromosomes 13, 14, 15, 16, 18, 21, X and Y. The assay utilizes fluorescently labeled primers to amplify chromosome-specific short tandem repeat (STR) markers. Peak area ratios are calculated to determine chromosome copy number. Sex chromosome analysis includes SRY and AMELY markers for Y chromosome detection, and multiple X-linked markers including AMELX and TAF9L (Xq21.1/3p24.2). The TAF9L marker provides quantitative assessment as it has homologous sequences on both X chromosome and chromosome 3p24.2.

RESULTS

Chromosome 13: Normal diallelic pattern detected (2 copies)
Chromosome 14: Normal diallelic pattern detected (2 copies)
Chromosome 15: Normal diallelic pattern detected (2 copies)
Chromosome 16: Normal diallelic pattern detected (2 copies)
Chromosome 18: Normal diallelic pattern detected (2 copies)
Chromosome 21: Normal diallelic pattern detected (2 copies)

Sex Chromosomes:
- X chromosome markers (AMELX, DXS6809, DXS6803): Single allele pattern consistent with one X chromosome
- Y chromosome markers (SRY, AMELY): No amplification detected
- TAF9L quantitative marker: Ratio 1:2 (X:autosome), confirming single X chromosome

CONCLUSION: 45,X - Monosomy X detected

INTERPRETATION
QF-PCR analysis demonstrates a single X chromosome with absence of Y-specific sequences, consistent with monosomy X (Turner syndrome). The quantitative TAF9L marker confirms the presence of only one X chromosome. Normal copy number is detected for chromosomes 13, 14, 15, 16, 18, and 21.

Monosomy X (45,X) is associated with Turner syndrome and is a common cause of first trimester pregnancy loss, accounting for approximately 10-15% of all spontaneous miscarriages. The majority of 45,X conceptuses (>99%) result in spontaneous loss. This finding likely explains the fetal demise in this case.

This represents a sporadic aneuploidy event with low recurrence risk for future pregnancies (approximately 1%).

RECOMMENDATIONS
1. Genetic counseling is recommended to discuss these results, provide emotional support, and review reproductive options
2. Optional parental chromosome analysis is available if desired, though parental chromosomal rearrangements are rarely associated with 45,X
3. Standard prenatal screening is recommended for future pregnancies

ASSAY LIMITATIONS
- This test detects whole chromosome aneuploidies only and will not detect balanced rearrangements, mosaicism below 20%, or single gene disorders
- Maternal cell contamination may affect results; however, the finding of monosomy X makes this unlikely
- This assay does not analyze chromosomes 1-12, 17, 19, 20, or 22

Reported by: [redacted name], PhD, FACMG
Laboratory Director: [redacted name], MD, PhD
